title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Aisha Banerjee
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the Product Overview, PRD (requirements), Design Specifications, Roadmap & Themes, Pricing & Packaging guidance, and Release Notes for Redwood Inference’s Unified Inference initiative. The goal of Unified Inference is to provide a single, consistent developer experience and runtime across Hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated, and Private deployments while exposing cost/performance controls that let customers optimize unit economics without sacrificing latency or reliability.

Audience
- Product managers, engineering leads, solutions and sales engineers, and stakeholders involved in go-to-market with Dedicated and Private.

Goals and Success Metrics
- Primary goals:
  1) Single API surface for text, chat, embeddings, and reranking across all deployment modes.
  2) Deterministic latency SLOs: 95th percentile tail latency <= configured SLO (see SLO table below).
  3) 20–40% reduction in per-token cost for typical PLG workloads through batching, caching, and quantization recommendations.
  4) Clear upgrade/rollback and model routing policies for graceful degradation.
- Success metrics (measured at product launch + quarterly):
  - Adoption: >= 30% of new Dedicated customers choose Unified Inference config within first 60 days.
  - Cost efficiency: mean per-token cost savings >= 25% on benchmark workloads vs baseline.
  - Reliability: customers see >= 99.9% availability for Dedicated; Hosted targets subject to tier.

Key Features (at launch)
- Unified REST/SDK API with backward-compatible routes and expanded streaming and function-calling support.
- Model catalog with verified performance profiles and recommended quantization profiles per workload.
- Smart routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, region affinity, and customer-tier policies.
- Automated prefix/KV caching with customer-configurable TTLs.
- Cost-aware controls exposed in Console: suggested batch sizes, quantization profiles, and caching policies.
- Rollouts: canary and A/B deploys, automatic fallback to compatible model variant when capacity constrained.

PRD: Requirements (MUST / SHOULD / MAY)
- MUST: Provide a unified endpoint for generation and embeddings with identical semantics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (API compatibility matrix included).
- MUST: Achieve 95th percentile latency SLOs configurable per-customer (default SLOs listed in the SLO table).
- MUST: Support kv-cache prefix caching with eviction policy and tracing hooks for diagnostics.
- MUST: Provide model variants and automated fallback policies; fallback must preserve tokenization compatibility.
- SHOULD: Suggest quantization and batching profiles using offline workload analysis and expose them as single-click suggestions in Console.
- SHOULD: Offer per-route per-token cost estimation in the Console and API responses (estimated_cost_cents field).
- MAY: Provide an SDK helper to auto-select routing strategy (cost vs latency) based on user-specified budget/latency targets.

API Compatibility Matrix (summary)
- Endpoint: /v1/generate — supported parameters: model, prompt, max_tokens, temperature, streaming, functions, metadata.
- Endpoint: /v1/embeddings — supported parameters: model, input, batch_id.
- Backward compatibility: parameters deprecated in 2025 are still accepted for two release cycles with warnings.

Design Specifications
- Runtime requirements:
  - The serving runtime must support continuous batching with dynamic batch size up to 1024 tokens aggregated across up to 256 concurrent requests.
  - Kernel selection layer must choose quantized kernels when model profile indicates <0.5% quality delta for the target prompt set.
  - KV cache consistency: caches are per-tenant and use strong consistency for Dedicated and eventual for Hosted (with detectable drift and automatic healing).

- Model catalog & profile format (example):
  - Fields (flat list): model_id, architecture, default_sequence_len, verified_batching_profile, recommended_quantization_profile, latency_p95_ms_at_32_tokens_on_V100.
  - Profiles are versioned with semantic versioning and immutable once published.

- Console UX notes:
  - Route view shows per-route token breakdown, top prompts by cost, and suggested optimization actions.
  - One-click apply for suggested quantization/batching must create an A/B canary change with automated rollback on quality regressions detected by evaluation hooks.

Roadmap & Themes (next 12 months)
- Q2 2026 (Immediate)
  - GA of Unified Inference core API and Console integration for Hosted + Dedicated pilots.
  - Release of model profiling service and first set of quantization recommendations.
  - Initial pricing tiers published for Dedicated reserved capacity.
- Q3 2026
  - Private deployment V1: air-gapped install with KMS integration and audit logging.
  - Expanded routing policies with multi-region failover.
  - Cost-analytics: per-customer cost-heatmaps and forecasted spend with suggested optimizations.
- Q4 2026
  - Autoscaling policies for Dedicated with burst capacity options.
  - Advanced rollouts: progressive canaries driven by real-time eval metrics.
  - Marketplace packaging and GA for Private for select enterprise customers.

Prioritization themes
- Reliability and predictable SLAs first.
- Cost efficiency second (measurable ROI).
- Developer ergonomics third (reduce friction to adopt).

Pricing & Packaging Notes
- Hosted API: continue usage-based pricing for generation and embeddings. The consumer experience and pricing math are unchanged; we will surface suggested optimizations in the Console to reduce cost.
- Dedicated (Reserved Capacity):
  - Packaging: monthly and annual reserved instances with three tiers: Standard (baseline), Business (SLA + priority routing), Enterprise (SLA + private control plane + extended retention).
  - Pricing guidance (example levels):
    | Tier | Commit | Monthly Price / GPU (est) | Notes |
    |------|--------|---------------------------|-------|
    | Standard | 1 GPU | $3,500/mo | Best-effort throughput SLAs |
    | Business | 10 GPU | $3,200/mo | 99.9% uptime, priority routing |
    | Enterprise | 50+ GPU | Custom | Private control plane, premium support |
- Dedicated add-ons:
  - Extended observability retention (30/90/365 days).
  - On-prem cluster support (packaging + airgap install).
  - Model validation and onboarding assistance as a consulting engagement.
- Private: license + support fee with optional managed control plane. Pricing to be negotiated per-customer (standard template available in Sales Ops).

Packaging & Billing Considerations
- Metering: tokens, embedding units, and model-hours for reserved capacity. Reserved capacity discounts apply to model-hours only; token billing still applies for burst traffic beyond reserved throughput.
- Billing transparency: Console must show projected monthly bill and savings if suggested optimizations are applied.

Release Notes: Unified Inference v1.0 (2026-03-25)
- Release summary:
  - GA release of Unified Inference core API and Console features for Hosted and Dedicated pilot customers.
  - Model profiling and quantization suggestion engine v0.9 included.
- Notable fixes and changes:
  1) KV cache TTL configuration added to the API and Console.
  2) Fallback policy now guarantees tokenization compatibility across variants.
  3) Perf regressions observed in internal alpha (p95 spikes under load) addressed by improved batching heuristic.
- Known issues:
  - Private air-gapped installer V1 is in beta and not yet GA; see onprem-packaging doc for manual instructions.
  - Some customer workloads with highly variable prefix lengths may see less benefit from default batching; recommendations will improve in v1.1.

Rollout Plan and Launch Checklist
1) Documentation & quickstarts published in eng-developer-experience docs and quickstarts-and-templates.
2) Sales enablement: training for AE/SEs, updated pitch decks, and pricing calculator.
3) Pilot customers (3–5) onboarded to Dedicated pilot group; collect feedback and telemetry for 30 days.
4) GA announcement and marketing coordination; provide migration playbook for existing Dedicated customers.

Ownership, Support & SLOs
- Product owner: Aisha Banerjee.
- Engineering lead: Miguel Ortega.
- SRE & runtime owner: Ethan Wang.
- Support tiers: Standard (email, 72h SLA), Business (4h response), Enterprise (1h response + designated TAM).
- Default SLO table:
  | Environment | Availability SLO | Latency p95 default | Notes |
  |-------------|------------------|---------------------|-------|
  | Hosted (API) | 99.5% | 300ms @ 32 tokens | Tiered customers may have better SLOs |
  | Dedicated | 99.9% | 150ms @ 32 tokens | Configurable per-customer |
  | Private | 99.5% (operator-managed) | Customer-defined | Depends on on-prem infra |

Operational Runbook (high level)
- Detection:
  1) Console alert: sustained p95 latency > configured SLO for > 5 min.
  2) Error budget burn > 50% in 24h window.
- Triage steps:
  1) Check model routing and fallback logs; revert to previous model variant if fallback threshold crossed.
  2) Inspect batching/queue length metrics and GPU utilization.
  3) If bucketed to Dedicated clusters: increase burst capacity on-call runbook step (requires infra approval).
  4) Engage oncall runtime + SRE.
- Rollback criteria:
  - Latency regressions > 30% over baseline and error rate increase > 2x within 15 minutes.
